children: U.S. banks are set to kick off earnings season on Tuesday, with Goldman Sachs
, JPMorgan Chase
, Citigroup
, and Well Fargo's

reporting. Most large U.S. banks are expected to show year-over-year earnings growth in Q3 2026 even as capital markets activity eased from the unusually hot pace in Q2. The only bank in the group of 18 banks in the table below expected to post a year-over-year earnings decline is Huntington Bancorp
According to the analysts’ consensus estimates, the largest improvements are expected at JPMorgan Chase
for the global systemically important banks (GSIBs), up 17%; State Street
, up 32%, for the trust banks; and Citizens Financial Group
, up 32% for the large-cap regional banks.
The banks seeing upward consensus estimate revisions across all three time horizons (1-month, 3-month, and 6-month) are JPMorgan
, Wells Fargo
, all the trust banks, U.S. Bancorp
, Truist Financial
, and KeyCorp

Results from big banks’ capital markets-related businesses are likely to cool in the quarter as activity eased. The global markets environment won't be as robust in Q3 2026 as it was in Q2, which was a "lights-out quarter by any measure," Bank of America
Co-President Jim DeMare said at an investor conference in September.

BMO Capital Markets analyst Gerard Cassidy is slightly more optimistic. “Capital market revenues will be a focus for selected banks, and we expect to hear positive commentary on the Markets & Investment Banking businesses for a seasonally slow quarter,” he wrote in a note to clients.

Oppenheimer analyst Chris Kotowski is more skeptical of capital markets’ staying power. “No one, ourselves included, saw this surge coming, and it could recede just as unexpectedly,” he wrote in a note to clients. Thus, he has become more cautious on capital-markets-oriented banks, specifically Goldman Sachs
and Morgan Stanley
, which are trading well above average relative P/Es.
That tracks with the overall analyst consensus EPS revisions. Analysts have revised their estimates downward for Goldman
and Bank of America
in the past month, from three months ago, and from six months ago. The consensus for Morgan Stanley
was also revised lower in the past month and for the past three months.
“For the most part we think boring, plain vanilla commercial banks are the better place to be, particularly U.S. Bancorp
and PNC Financial Services
,” Oppenheimer’s Kotowski said.

Citi’s Benjamin Gerlinger also favors commercial banks. “We believe the best-positioned banks check the boxes of commercially focused (both loans and deposits), healthy capital bases, and limited credit concerns,” he wrote in a note to clients.
Last month, Citi upgraded Fifth Third
bank to Buy from Neutral, citing its setup for higher interest rates supporting overall repricing.
Citi also likes U.S. Bancorp
for positive EPS revisions and KeyCorp
on the basis that recent pressure points will reverse.

Jefferies bank analyst David Chiaverini expects the banks’ guidance for net interest income  “to be largely reiterated with a modest upward bias.” Growth is likely to come from increased volume rather than margin improvement, he added.

Furthermore, Jefferies expects the sector to face incremental pressure from higher deposit costs following the recent Fed hike, elevated deposit competition, and tighter loan spreads (particularly CRE), partially offset by ongoing fixed-rate asset repricing. Jefferies favors Bank of America
, Citigroup
, U.S. Bancorp
, Fifth Third Bancorp
, and Citizens Financial Group
heading into Q3 earnings season.

title: Watch big banks' capital markets, commercial banking results in Q3 earnings
